Rashi on Pesachim 69a:11:1.hebrew: דוחין את השבת - אפי' מלאכה גמורה, במס' שבת (דף קל.):
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:11:1.english: Override Shabbat - Even a full-fledged [prohibited] labor, in Tractate Shabbat (130a).

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:11:2.hebrew: היכא דגברא חזי - כגון להביא איזמל למילה דרך רשות הרבים, שכבר התינוק ראוי למול. אבל היכא דגברא לא חזי, כגון האי טמא, לא רמיא חיובא עליה, ואין אלו מכשירי מצוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:11:2.english: Where the person is fit - For example, bringing a knife for circumcision through a public domain, as the infant is already fit to be circumcised. But where the person is not fit, such as this impure [person], the obligation is not incumbent upon him, and these are not [considered] preliminaries of a mitzva.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:12:1.hebrew: אמר רבה לדברי רבי אליעזר - דאמר כל היכא דגברא לא חזי, ליכא חיובא עליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:12:1.english: Rabbah said: According to the words of Rabbi Eliezer - Who said [that] wherever a person is not fit, there is no obligation upon him.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:12:2.english: A healthy baby - For without washing, [he is] fit to be circumcised.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:12:3.english: One may heat warm water for him - On Shabbat, before circumcision.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:12:4.english: To strengthen him - To be healthy and strong.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:12:5.hebrew: קטן חולה - שכל זמן שלא ירחצוהו בחמין לא יראה למול, ואם ירחצוהו יראה למילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:12:5.english: A sickly baby - For as long as they do not bathe him in hot water, he is not fit to be circumcised, and if they bathe him, he is fit for circumcision.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:13:1.hebrew: הכל אצל מילה חולין הן - כל זמן שלא נרחצו בחמין, ואפילו לרבי אליעזר צריך להיות לו מחמי חמין מערב שבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:13:1.english: All [babies] are sickly with respect to circumcision - As long as they have not been washed in hot water; and even according to Rabbi Eliezer, he must have hot water [heated] from the eve of Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:14:1.english: Abaye raised an objection to him: An uncircumcised [man] - An adult who did not circumcise [himself] on the eve of Passover.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:14:2.hebrew: ענוש כרת - בשביל שהיה ראוי לתקן מו' שעות, מזמן דשחיטת הפסח ולמעלה, ולא ניתקן. ולא דמי לטמא ושהיה בדרך רחוקה, שאין יכולין לתקן באותן שש שעות, ומיקמי הכי לא רמיא חיובא עלייהו. אלמא, אע"ג דלא חזיא, רמיא מצוה עליה היכא דאפשר למיתקן; והזאה נמי תדחה שבת, דהא מצוה רמיא עליה ליתקן לכך. ואי קשיא הא דקיימא לן (לקמן פסחים דף צב.): "הפורש מן הערלה כפורש מן הקבר", וצריך הזאה שלישי ושביעי, ואפילו מל אינו ראוי — הא אוקמינן לההיא בערל נכרי שנתגייר בפרק האשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:14:2.english: Punished with karet - Because he was fit to rectify [himself] from six hours [of the day], from the time of slaughtering the Paschal lamb and onward, and he did not rectify [himself]. And he is not comparable to an impure person or one who was on a distant journey, who cannot rectify [their status] during those six hours, and prior to that, the obligation was not incumbent upon them. Apparently, even though he is not fit, the mitzva is incumbent upon him wherever it is possible to rectify [himself]; and sprinkling [the purification waters] should also override Shabbat, since the mitzva is incumbent upon him to rectify himself for this. And if you ask [regarding] that which we hold (later, Pesachim 92a): "One who separates from the foreskin is like one who separates from the grave," and requires sprinkling on the third and seventh [days], so even if he circumcised he is not fit — [the answer is that] we have established that [teaching] as referring to an uncircumcised gentile who converted, in the chapter HaIsha.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:15:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: אמר רבה, קסבר <abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> אליעזר, אין שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:15:1.english: This is our reading [in the Gemara]: "Rabba said: Rabbi Eliezer holds [that] one may not slaughter [the Paschal lamb] and sprinkle [its blood] for someone who is ritually impure due to [contact with] a creeping animal."

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:1:1.hebrew: ורבי אליעזר - אמר לך: האי לאו קל וחומר הוא, דשבות מצוה עדיפא משבות דרשות. הלכך, יום טוב דשמחתו רשות, גזרו על שבות שלה; אבל שבת, דדחיית מלאכה שבו משום מצוה היא, לא גזרו חכמים בה על השבות לדחות את המצוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:1:1.english: And Rabbi Eliezer - [He would] say to you: This is not a kal vachomer [a fortiori inference], for a shevut [rabbinic prohibition] of a mitzvah is preferable to a shevut of an optional matter. Therefore, [on] a festival, whose rejoicing is optional, they decreed regarding its shevut; however, [on] Shabbat, where the overriding of labor on it is for the sake of a mitzvah, the Sages did not decree regarding the shevut on it [so as] to push aside the mitzvah.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:2:1.hebrew: שלאחר שחיטה - מיחוי קרביו, ואע"ג דאיתעביד ליה צורך גבוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:2:1.english: After the slaughter - [This refers to] rinsing its innards, even though the need of the Most High has [already] been performed.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:2:2.hebrew: לא ידחו כו' - בתמיה, למיעבד צורכי גבוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:2:2.english: Do they not override, etc. - [This is said] as a rhetorical question: [should they not override Shabbat] to perform the needs of the Most High?

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:3:1.hebrew: דמה לי - כלומר, דין הוא כן, ומה לי לתמוה? שהרי דחתה שחיטה כבר את שבת במצותה. הלכך, הואיל וניתנה לדחות כבר, לא גזרו בה שוב על שבות הצריך:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:3:1.english: For what is it to me - That is to say, this is logical, and what is there for me to wonder about? For slaughter has already overridden Shabbat through its mitzvah; therefore, since [Shabbat] has already been permitted to be overridden, they did not further decree regarding it [prohibiting] a rabbinic prohibition [shevut] that is necessary [for it].

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:4:1.hebrew: ברישא - אמר ליה האי טעמא, שמא ימצא זבח פסול:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:4:1.english: At first - [Rabbi Akiva] said to him this reason: "perhaps the offering will be found [to be] invalid."

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:4:2.hebrew: ופרכיה - ואמר ליה: א"כ, משחט נמי לא נשחוט:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:4:2.english: And he refuted it - And [Rabbi Eliezer] said to him: "If so, we should also not slaughter [the offering]."

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:5:1.hebrew: בשחיטה השבתני - דבר שחוק וגיחוך שאמרת: "או חילוף, ומה אם הזאה שהיא שבות אינה דוחה — שחיטה לא כל שכן שלא תדחה?!" ובאת לעקור את מה שכתוב בו "במועדו", ויודע היית שאין זה ק"ו:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:5:1.english: With slaughter you have answered me - [This is] a matter of mockery and derision that you said: "Or the reverse: if sprinkling, which is [only] a rabbinic prohibition, does not override [Shabbat], all the more so should slaughter not override [it]!" And you came to uproot that which is written concerning it, "in its appointed time," while you knew that this is not a [valid] a fortiori inference.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:5:2.hebrew: אל תכפירני - אל תכפור במה שלימדתני: הזאה, אע"פ שהיא שבות, אינה דוחה. ולכך דנתי קל וחומר זה לפניך, אע"פ שאינו כדאי, אלא כדי שתשים אל לבך: "אחרי שבא זה לדון שחיטה מהזאה, מכלל דבהזאה פשיטא ליה דלא דחיא". מתוך כך תזכור מה שלימדתני דלא דחיא, ותחזור בך ממה שאתה אומר "ועליה אני דן":
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:5:2.english: Do not deny me - Do not deny what you taught me: sprinkling, even though it is a shevut [rabbinic prohibition], does not override [Shabbat]. And for this reason I argued this kal vachomer [a fortiori inference] before you, even though it is not worthy [on its own], only so that you would take it to heart: "Since this one [i.e., I] came to derive slaughter from sprinkling, it follows that regarding sprinkling it is obvious to him that it does not override [Shabbat]." Through this you will remember what you taught me, that it does not override [Shabbat], and you will retract what you say, "And concerning it I argue."

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:5:3.english: At the time of the argument - At this time when we are arguing about it.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:6:1.hebrew: ומאחר דאגמריה - ר' אליעזר גופיה דלא דחיא, מאי טעמא פריך ואמר "עליה אני דן":
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:6:1.english: And since he taught him - [Since] Rabbi Eliezer himself [taught him] that [sprinkling] does not override [Shabbat], why did he challenge [him] and say, "Against it I argue"?

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:6:2.hebrew: הזאה דתרומה - הבא להזות עליו ליטהר כדי לאכול תרומה, אגמריה דלא דחיא שבת, דהא הפרשת תרומה גופא לא דחיא שבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:6:2.english: Sprinkling of teruma - [Regarding one who] comes to have [purifying water] sprinkled upon him to become pure in order to eat teruma — [this is what] he taught him does not override Shabbat, since separating teruma itself does not override Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:8:1.hebrew: הזאת טמא מת כו' - אלמא דבהזאת פסח השיבו וקאמר אינה דוחה שבת. אלמא דאגמריה ר' אליעזר דאינה דוחה, מדפשיטא ליה כולי האי:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:8:1.english: The sprinkling of one impure from a corpse, etc. - Thus, he answered him regarding the sprinkling for the Paschal lamb, and he says [that] it does not override Shabbat. Thus, R. Eliezer taught him that it does not override [Shabbat], since it is so obvious to him.

Rashi on Pesachim 69a:9:1.hebrew: אלא ודאי הזאת פסח אגמריה - ומאי גזירת שבות איכא בהזאה? גזירה שמא יעבירנה בידו. וכשהיה דן עליה עם ר' עקיבא, שכח דבר זה מלמודו. והכי נמי אמרינן בע"א בפרק כל הצלמים (עבודה זרה דף מו:): ר' אליעזר גמריה איעקר ליה, ואתא ר' עקיבא לאדכוריה גמריה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69a:9:1.english: Rather, [he] certainly taught him [the law of] sprinkling [for] the Paschal lamb - And what rabbinic decree of shevut is there in sprinkling? [It is] a decree lest he carry it in his hand [in the public domain]. When he was debating it with Rabbi Akiva, he forgot this matter from his learning. And so too do we say in [Tractate] Avodah Zarah, in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaTzelamim (Avodah Zarah 46b): Rabbi Eliezer forgot his teaching, and Rabbi Akiva came to remind him of his teaching.

Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:10:1.hebrew: שמא יעבירנה ארבע אמות - וא"ת: ואמאי חיישינן להכי, הלא נושא מי חטאת טמא ויחזור ויטמא את המים? ויש לומר, דמעביר בכלי אבנים ובכלי גללים דלא מקבלי טומאה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:10:1.english: Lest he carry it four cubits - And if you say: Why are we concerned about this? Behold, one who carries purification water [becomes] impure, and he will in turn render the water impure! One can answer that he carries [it] in stone vessels or in dung vessels, which are not susceptible to ritual impurity.

Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:12:1.hebrew: קטן בריא מחמין כו' דהא חזי - דווקא לר' אליעזר יש חילוק בין חזי ללא חזי, אבל ר' עקיבא אינו מחלק כלל, דהא קאמר במתני': "הזאה תוכיח":
Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:12:1.english: "A healthy baby, one may heat [water], etc., as he is fit" - Specifically according to Rabbi Eliezer is there a distinction between [one who is] fit and [one who is] not fit, whereas Rabbi Akiva does not distinguish at all, for he says in the Mishnah: "Sprinkling will prove [it]."

Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:13:1.hebrew: לא שנא חלש ולא שנא בריא אין מחמין לו חמין כו' - וכי אמר רבי אליעזר דמכשירי מילה דחו שבת, ה"מ היכא שהוחמו חמין מערב שבת, דחזי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:13:1.english: Whether [the baby is] sickly or healthy, one may not heat water for him, etc. - And when Rabbi Eliezer says that the preliminaries of circumcision override Shabbat, that applies where hot water was heated on Shabbat eve, for [then he is] fit [for circumcision].

Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:15:1.hebrew: שוחטין וזורקין כו' - וא"ת: אי שוחטי' וזורקי' על טמא שרץ, אמאי כתב רחמנא טמא אינו עושה פסח? פשיטא! דהא כתיב "איש לפי אכלו" לעכב, דבעינן גברא דחזי לאכילה, כדמוכח בכיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים עח:). ונראה לרשב"א דאיצטריך לאשמעינן דחייב בפסח שני, דלא נימא דמיפטר משום דשני תשלומין דראשון הוא — דחזי בראשון חזי בשני, דלא חזי בראשון לא חזי בשני, כדאמר לקמן גבי חגיגה בכיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים פ.). אי נמי, איצטריך למימרא דציבור עבדי בטומאה, כדדרשינן: "איש כי יהיה טמא" — איש נדחה, ואין ציבור נדחין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:15:1.english: [One may not] slaughter and sprinkle, etc. - And if you ask: If we [do] slaughter and sprinkle for one who is impure from a creeping creature, why did the Merciful One write [that] an impure person does not make the Pesach [offering]? It is obvious [that one who remains impure cannot make it], for it is written, "each man according to his eating," as an essential requirement — that we require a person who is fit for eating [at night], as is proven in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (below, Pesachim 78b)! And it appears to the Rashba that [the verse] is needed to teach us that he is obligated in the second Pesach, so that we should not say that he is exempt because the second [Pesach] is a compensation for the first [Pesach] — [such that] whoever is fit for the first is fit for the second, [and] whoever is not fit for the first is not fit for the second, as [the Gemara] says below regarding the Chagigah offering in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (below, Pesachim 80a). Alternatively, it is needed to state that the community makes [the Pesach offering] in [a state of] impurity, as we expound: "If any man shall be impure" — an individual is deferred [to the second Pesach], but a community is not deferred:

Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:3:1.hebrew: אם דחו מכשירי מצוה שלאחר שחיטה השבת כו' - פי' בקונטרס: מיחוי קרביו. ותימה לר"י: מה ראיה מייתי? דילמא שאני התם משום דלא אפשר למיעבד מאתמול. ונראה לר"י, דמכשירי מצוה שלאחר שחיטה דקאמר — היינו הקטר חלבים, דאפשר להמתין עד הלילה ודחי שבת. וכן יש בירושלמי, דקא אמר ר' אליעזר: "אימורי ציבור יוכיחו, אע"פ שאפשר להמתין למוצאי שבת; מה לי מכשירין שלאחר שחיטה כו'". והא דפריך "משחט נמי לא לשחוט", אע"ג דשחיטה לא אפשר — מ"מ פריך, משום שכבר הוכיח שאין חילוק בין אפשר ללא אפשר, מדשרינן הקטר חלבים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:3:1.english: If actions that facilitate the mitzva after the slaughter override Shabbat, etc. - Rashi explained: rinsing its innards. And Rabbi Yitzchak finds [this] surprising: What proof does [Rabbi Eliezer] bring [from there]? Perhaps it is different there because it is impossible to do [it] from yesterday [before Shabbat]. And it appears to Rabbi Yitzchak that "actions that facilitate the mitzva after the slaughter" that he mentions refers to the burning of the fats, for it is possible to wait until nightfall [after Shabbat], and [yet] it overrides Shabbat. And so it is in the Jerusalem Talmud, where Rabbi Eliezer says: "The sacrificial parts of communal [offerings] prove [it], even though it is possible to wait until after Shabbat; what is the difference to me [between] actions that facilitate [the mitzva] after the slaughter, etc." And [as for] that which [Rabbi Eliezer] objects, "It should also not be slaughtered" — even though slaughter cannot [be done before Shabbat], nevertheless he objects [to Rabbi Akiva's reasoning], because he has already proven that there is no distinction between what is possible [to defer] and what is not possible, from the fact that we permit the burning of the fats [on Shabbat].

Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:6:1.hebrew: הזאה דתרומה אגמריה - ואית לן למימר דר' אליעזר הי' סבור דבהזאה דפסח קאמר ר"ע, ולכך היה משיב "ועליה אני דן" שתהא מותרת, דהשתא סבירא לן דהזאה דפסח דחיא שבת. וקאמר ליה ר"ע: "זה חילוף", שהיה סבור שר' אליעזר היה טועה במה שלמדו דאינה דוחה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:6:1.english: "He taught him [regarding] sprinkling for terumah" - And we must say that Rabbi Eliezer thought that Rabbi Akiva was speaking about sprinkling for the Paschal offering, and therefore he [Rabbi Eliezer] would reply, "And concerning it I argue" that it should be permitted — for now we hold that sprinkling for the Paschal offering overrides Shabbat. And Rabbi Akiva said to him, "This is a reversal," because he [Rabbi Akiva] thought that Rabbi Eliezer was mistaken about what he had taught him — that it does not override [Shabbat].

Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:6:2.hebrew: דתרומה גופה לא דחיא שבת - וא"ת, נילף דתידחי שבת מכל הנהו? וי"ל: משום דיכול לקיים מצות אכילת תרומה אחר השבת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 69a:6:2.english: Because teruma itself does not override Shabbat - And if you ask: Let us derive that it should override Shabbat from all those [other cases]? One can answer: Because one can fulfill the mitzvah of eating teruma after Shabbat.
